patch_description:
Key idea: reduce parameter count and inject geometry-aware high-order motifs aligned with tic‑tac‑toe winning lines while preserving expressive entangling and local rotations. I restore a symmetry-grouped EfficientSU2-like layout that previously achieved stronger validation/test accuracy: (1) shared RY rotations per symmetry zone (corners, edges, center) to reduce redundant parameters, (2) CRZ entanglers around the outer ring with a separate shared center coupling to propagate radial correlations, (3) ZZZ three-qubit rotations explicitly placed on the eight winning lines so the circuit can directly form winning-line correlations, (4) two CCRZ patterns for compressed higher-order correlations, and (5) compact final rotations (shared RZ+RX per zone) to keep parameter count low but allow local phase flexibility.

Why this should improve performance:
- Parameter efficiency: sharing across symmetric qubits reduces N_PARAMS (to 78) which helps generalization and parameter_efficiency metric.
- Motif alignment: placing ZZZ on the winning lines gives the optimizer direct primitives to capture 3-body patterns crucial for the task, aiding accuracy and faster convergence.
- Balanced entanglement: CRZ ring + center couplings spreads information across the grid without excessive distinct parameters, reducing train-test gap.
- Compact final rotations provide local flexibility without exploding parameter count.

All other training settings (Adam, re-uploading layout, feature map, n_uploads/n_repeats, measurements) are unchanged to allow fair comparison.
